data.review_body:
DONT BUY FROM ALIEXPRESS NEVER EVER 


Subject: Formal Complaint Regarding Faulty Phone and Inadequate Refund

Dear AliExpress Customer Service,

I am writing to make a formal complaint regarding an iPhone 17 Pro that I purchased through your platform.

The phone I received is faulty. From the first day of use, the mobile network has repeatedly gone on and off, making it impossible to make reliable calls or use mobile data. The phone is not working properly and is not fit for its intended purpose.

I contacted customer service to request a full refund because the product is defective. However, I was only offered a partial refund of £35, even though I paid £90 for the phone.

This partial refund is not a fair resolution. With £35, I cannot purchase a replacement phone. A working phone with similar features would cost at least £70, meaning I would still be left significantly out of pocket because I received a faulty product.

Under consumer protection principles, when a product arrives defective or is not as described, the customer should not be expected to bear the financial loss. I therefore request one of the following resolutions:

A full refund of the £90 purchase price upon returning the faulty phone, or
A replacement phone that is fully functional and matches the description of the item I purchased.
I hope this matter can be resolved promptly and fairly. If a satisfactory solution cannot be reached, I will consider escalating my complaint through the appropriate dispute resolution process and, if applicable, through my payment provider.

I look forward to your prompt response.

Yours faithfully,

Mohammad Mazed D ALam
Order Number:  3071421789104415
Purchase Date: April 2026
data.review_headline: DONT BUY FROM ALIEXPRESS NEVER EVER

data.review_body:
"The products arrived fine, but the platform's tax calculator & customer-support is complete nightmare.

I placed 2 separate orders (total 4 items across 2 product categories). Their previous system inflated the cost as they included flat 3€ custom duty on all products. AliExpress consolidated all items into ONE single package. Under EU/IOSS rules, the flat €3 custom fee should be charged per product category (€3 x 2 = €6). Instead, now their system had charged €3 for every individual item (€3 x 4 = €12), effectively double-charging me on import taxes, which were never refunded.

To make matters worse, customer support is a complete brick wall. Because the package was pre-paid via IOSS, it cleared customs automatically—meaning local customs release invoices & other documents literally do not exist. Yet, same scripted support has already demanded 'these invoices and documents' that don't exist in this universe 5–7 times in a row even after I already provided proof that I was overcharged. 

Buyers beware!!!: You will be trapped in an endless Circus-clown show loop being asked to prove taxes even if they were collected directly by AliExpress in the first place & documents everyone knows aren't real thing". Whether this is a gross deliberate tactic to pocket extra fees or pure platform incompetence: BE EXTREMELY CAREFUL with AliExpress tax calculations! If their system miscalculates your tax, getting a refund is simply impossible
data.review_headline: AliExpress overcharging customs taxes > Support refuses to refund overcharge and fix their mistakes

data.review_body:
I bought an item that was listed as brand new and described as being in stock, with 992 units available. I trusted the seller and purchased it for £145, plus shipping.
Unfortunately, the item I received was faulty. It also showed clear signs of having been previously used and repaired. Although I was still able to use it to some extent, it was essentially scrap and certainly not a new product.
I contacted the seller several times and also reported the issue to AliExpress through multiple levels of their dispute and reporting process. However, my claim was rejected. AliExpress replied that the listing did not violate their platform policies.
This means that, according to AliExpress's decision, sellers can advertise an item as brand new while supplying a used, repaired, or faulty product without the listing being considered a violation of the platform's rules.
data.review_headline: Sold as new, received as faulty and sign of used and repaired

I took a partial refund of just over $21.00.  This experience is discracedul.  Do they do this deliberately?  I do not know but their return policy is discracedul.  I would never buy from them again or recommend this company to 
anyone else.  Be warned.  Steer clear.
